x: On the outward journey Ray Hall and John Knifton led the field with Paul Nihill (S.W.C) in close attendance. After the turn at Banstead Ray Hall took the lead from John Knifton, but in the later stages Nihill came through strongly and finished a worthy winner while John managed to snatch second plac…

Ray was in very fine form and he managed to pull back Paul Nihill who was leading at one stage, and then went on to beat him by 1:41. Ray Hall (4th) John Knifton (5th) W.Belderson (7th) backed extremely well and we managed to retain the County Team Championship by the narrow margin of 2 points from Surrey W.C.

The individual race was well and truly won by Paul Nihill (Surrey WC) who had a margin of some 47 secs on the second man home Bob Clark (Poly) with Arthur Thomson (Met.WC) just easing himself into third spot.

This time it was Paul Nihill of Surrey that came between Vaughan Thomas and victory. Behind Vaughan our lads packed excellently although perhaps a little too far down for we were beaten for first place by Metropolitan WC.
Ray Hall "out for a quickie" finished 9th in 55:53 with Belderson three minutes down in 17th position. Vaugham Thomas and Paul Nihill were both 'pulled'.
Vaughan Thomas had to give second best to Paul Nihill at Regents Park but had the satisfaction of beating Edgington of Coventry who finished ahead of him in the National "10".

Paul Nihill slammed the old course record with his time of 2:25.38 and so well did Vaughan Thomas walk that, despite being some 6 mins. behind his great rival, he was also inside the previous best figures.
Vaughan Thomas was again in good form when he continued his 'battle for supremacy' with his Surrey W.C. rival, Paul Nihill in the Southern Area 20 Kilos.

Although Ray Middleton (Bels) our National Champion was amongst the starters this race wes just a training spin for him after a lay off, so it was left to Paul Nihill (S.W.C) to provide the main opposition to Pamich.

On a fine afternoon Paul Nihill of Surrey Walking Club, swept into an immediate lead which he steadily increased throughout the whole of the race from John Edgington, the International walker from Coventry and Peter McCullagh of Metropolitan W.C., Oxford University, and Australia.
Paul Nihill walked beautifully to win from his clubmate Fullager (M) with Eric Hall a creditable third. 4th January 1964 - The Juniors entered a team in the Essex Beagles Open 3¾.
The Southern Counties AAA '7' track championship was held at Battersea Park on March 7th. P. Nihill (SWC) was the winner in a record breaking 51:44.

After the first few miles Paul Nihill (S.W.C) led from Ray, and near the halfway mark tried to increase his lead; but to no avail. Gradually Ray crept nearer until he passed to take the lead and from then on was never headed; Paul Nihill dropping out eventually before Lewes.
(Photo:Ed Lacey) The start of the Olympic 50 Kilos at Tokyo showing, ringed, (L.to R.) Ray Middleton, Don Thompson and Paul Nihill, the silver medallist.
Fullager's win over his club-mate, Olympic silver medallist P.
After a little over 1½ hours walking Surrey W.C's Paul Nihill had annexed another RWA title; both individual and team. With Eric Hall in our team we could have been runners-up but, as it was, Met.

Ray Middleton and Surrey's Olympic medallist Paul Nihill made a fight of it for a large part of the way with Nihill only 22 secs ahead at half-way and the threat of a strong Middleton finish, but Nihill drew away half way up Copse Hill near the end and increased his lead to a minute.

His time was 53:51.4, 1:40 behind winner Paul Nihill (S.W.C) Adrian Major finished 32nd in the Junior Inter-Counties race at Derby on March 11th and was second man to finish in the second-placed Surrey team.
Bright spot was Ray Middleton's second place in the Surrey event. Winner was "retired" Olympic medallist Paul Nihill.

Paul Nihill of Surrey went away from the start but at 3 miles Ronny Wallwork overtook him and shortly afterwards the Surrey man was pulled. Further back Ray Middleton and Bob Barnes were moving through steadily after a cautious start with Eric and Ray Hall well placed not far behind.

But it is reasonable to think that no athlete of any branch of athletics received a greater tribute than did Jose Pedraza from Mexico when he was given the first prize by the President, Ted Stimpson for winning the Belgrave Open Walk in the fast time of 50m.21s., P.

43 Walkers took this opportunity to work off their Christmas excesses with Paul Nihill leading them home in 52.42. Gerry Cameron improved on his recent form to take the Handicap with an actual time of 57.43

Walking superbly Paul Nihill took no less than 1½ minutes off Stan Vicker's record. Ray Middleton and Bob Barnes both recorded fast times but it was Carl Lawton, with a personal best, who pulled Belgrave through into second place behind an apparently unbeatable Met WC Team.

Pat Duncan was beaten into second place at Steyning by Arthur Jones although his time 2.58 odd was a big improvement. In the Surrey Ray Middleton was content to take it easy behind an inspired Paul Nihill who improves every time out.
Paul Nihill, Tokyo Silver medallist, Lightman and Eley had all shown themselves to be in tremendous form but with 13 laps to endure our Ray Middleton's reliability was likely to prove useful.
Wesch (Belgrave) and the eventual winner Paul Nihill (Surrey WC).
It's Percy Wilson leading Olympian Paul Nihill in the R.W.A.
Nearly a clean sweep for Belgrave in the Surrey County Track Walks. The senior was won by Paul Nihill from Wil Wesch, Paul Duckett took the junior and Andy Hinchcliff walked off with the youth title.
Paul Nihill's great win in the 20 Kilos Walk tended to overshadow Britain's performance in the 50 Kilos event when two of our trio were unable to finish.

Bob Coates hung grimly to Paul Nihill from the gun but it was too good to last and at four mile Bob was pulled out. John Moullin also failed to satisfy the judges but with steady walking from our leading four the race was ours.
On the second leg Wilf Wesch took over from Pat and attacked Paul Nihill's 1963 record with a ferocity which left it shattered by some two minutes.

Wil Wesch surrandered his 3,000m. walk title to in-form Paul Nihill, but in doing so helped his rival to a new world best performance. Bob Coates showed good form after a spell away from competition to take third place, and with Carl Lawton fourth and Dave DeBondi sixth, it was a pity there was no team race.
A notable absentee from the Surrey race was Paul Nihill who was returning a World best 69:00 for 10 miles in the Isle of Man. Second place was taken by Belgrave's Alan Callow in 74:50.
But even so, Surrey, with a score of 23, looked very strong, with four in the first 11 (individual scoring). The race was a triumph for Paul Nihill, as well as his club?
Surrey saw Carl Lawton recording a personal best on a fair course and still finishing second as Paul Nihill blasted off one of the fastest 20s ever.
Just as it seemed that RAY would fill the vacant third spot the Board announced that Paul Nihill would "double up" and do the 50 kilos as well as the 20 kilos.

Carl took the initiative and in his finest race to date pushed Paul Nihill very hard for much of the distance. Carl was overtaken by Bob Dobson in the closing stages but hung on to beat 4 hours 20 minutes and gain selection for the European Games.
WIL WESCH (1), selected for West Germany in the 20 Kilos walk at the Olympic Games, Munich 1972, leads British international Paul Nihill in the Surrey County 3,000m track championship of 1971.
Paul Nihill scorched off in search of a British record but faded badly near the end. Carl Lawton managed to complete the distance although far short of his best road performance.
On a tough two lap course Paul Nihill turned in a class performance to see the rest of the field trailing far behind. The best that Carl Lawton could produce was 7th.
Meanwhile over at Croydon, Allan Callow was finishing 3rd behind Paul Nihill in a 20 kilo's race.
Len Duquemin walked steadily home for 4th. The final race, the 3km, was an easy victory for Paul Nihill with Carl Lawton a distant 2nd.
In his last race before emigrating to New Zealand, Allan Callow finished 2nd in 97:37 to Paul Nihill (Croydon) 90:07 over 20 kilometres.

As the field settled down to tackle the uphill slog to Warlingham they were led by Paul Nihill and Carl Lawton, then along past Chelsham and Farleigh to the half-way mark where Paul was opening up a lead.
Roger Mills of Ilford provided something of a sensation when he was 'pulled' on the very first lap going for a super-fast time. Paul Nihill won in 12:43.2

Championships in 12:33.2, breaking Paul Nihill's record by seven seconds, he has also led the field to the finish in the Enfield 20km (91:01), the Ilford 10km (43:09) and the Lambeth 10km (44:43). 1977 has seen Graham emerge as one of the main contenders for the Commonwealth Games in Edmonton, Canada next year.
